raw_response:
C12 — catalogue baseline B
Decision cutoff: 2016-09-08

I found four transferable candidates. These are proposed design inputs, not claims of deployment or demonstrated benefit in the requested interpreter.

1. Truffle Assumption dependency invalidation
https://chrisseaton.com/truffleruby/pldi17-truffle/pldi17-truffle.pdf
Truffle can attach optimized code to a binding-stability assumption and invalidate that code on mutation, avoiding repeated checks in compiled execution. Scope: relatively stable builtins, globals, and type bindings. Caveat: every mutation must trigger the right dependencies, and deoptimization or recompilation has a cost. The opened primary paper is from June 2017, so this is later evidence.
Discovery catalogue: https://github.com/wdv4758h/awesome-jit

2. V8 hidden classes and dependent-code invalidation
https://v8.dev/docs/hidden-classes
V8 supplies a model for caching attribute locations and invalidating optimized constant-property reads when the underlying property changes. Scope: object and type attributes, with further adaptation for namespace bindings. Caveat: stable shape does not imply stable value, and Python lookup behavior must still be preserved. The live page is undated; availability by the cutoff is unknown.
Discovery catalogue: https://github.com/wdv4758h/awesome-jit

3. RPython tracing guards and interpreter fallback
https://rpython.readthedocs.io/en/latest/jit/pyjitpl5.html
RPython provides a guard-and-fallback framework for abandoning a specialization when a checked assumption about a mutable namespace fails. Scope: the execution and recovery path around cached names. Caveat: these notes do not provide a cheap dictionary-change detector; checking cost still needs design. Historical availability is unknown because the live notes are undated and both attempted historical sources failed.
Discovery catalogue: https://github.com/wdv4758h/awesome-jit

4. Azure Cache-Aside invalidation flow
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/azure/architecture/patterns/cache-aside
The Cache-Aside pattern offers a concrete miss, refill, and write-invalidation flow for a namespace lookup cache. Scope: entry lifecycle and fallback lookup. Caveat: the distributed pattern permits stale reads, whereas Python requires synchronous handling of every relevant mutation; only the lifecycle transfers directly. The opened live catalogue entry is undated.
Discovery catalogue: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/azure/architecture/patterns/cache-aside

LuaJIT was investigated but omitted because the opened overview and FAQ did not establish its relevant invalidation mechanism. No target proposal page or recognized target-proposal citation was used. The run used seven catalogue-restricted search queries and stopped at 25 charged open/click attempts: 22 pages opened, one blocked, one missing, and one fetch error. No candidate has verified pre-cutoff evidence in this run.
